arguments.content: The problem we address is the inefficiency and scalability limitations in distributed machine learning systems when processing large-scale heterogeneous data across multiple nodes. Existing systems often fail to balance computation and communication overhead effectively, leading to suboptimal performance and resource utilization.

payload.original_content: draft_proposal_section({'proposal_id': 'PROP-7', 'drafter_id': 'uma', 'section': 'importance', 'content': 'Addressing inefficiency and scalability in distributed machine learning systems is critically important due to the increasing volume and diversity of data generated in real-world applications. Enhancing these systems facilitates faster, more accurate model training and deployment, which benefits AI-driven technologies in healthcare, finance, and autonomous systems. arguments.content: Addressing inefficiency and scalability in distributed machine learning systems is critically important due to the increasing volume and diversity of data generated in real-world applications. Enhancing these systems facilitates faster, more accurate model training and deployment, which benefits AI-driven technologies in healthcare, finance, and autonomous systems. Improving performance directly impacts cost reduction and energy efficiency, which are essential for sustainable and practical ML solutions.

payload.original_content: draft_proposal_section({'proposal_id': 'PROP-7', 'drafter_id': 'saanvi', 'section': 'difficulty', 'content': 'The difficulty lies in effectively modeling and mitigating the impact of statistical heterogeneity (Non-IID data) in federated learning systems without significantly increasing computational or communication overhead on individual nodes. arguments.content: The difficulty lies in effectively modeling and mitigating the impact of statistical heterogeneity (Non-IID data) in federated learning systems without significantly increasing computational or communication overhead on individual nodes. Balancing personalized models with generalization to global patterns requires novel algorithmic strategies and system design.

payload.original_content: draft_proposal_section({'proposal_id': 'PROP-7', 'drafter_id': 'tomas', 'section': 'gap', 'content': 'Current distributed machine learning systems inadequately address the gap of efficiently handling statistical heterogeneity at scale within resource-constrained environments. arguments.content: Current distributed machine learning systems inadequately address the gap of efficiently handling statistical heterogeneity at scale within resource-constrained environments. There is a lack of integrated approaches that simultaneously optimize communication efficiency, model personalization, and robustness to non-IID data across decentralized nodes, which remain open research challenges limiting practical deployment.

payload.original_content: draft_proposal_section({'proposal_id': 'PROP-7', 'drafter_id': 'uma', 'section': 'approach', 'content': 'We propose a hybrid federated learning framework that integrates adaptive communication protocols with personalized model updates to efficiently mitigate statistical heterogeneity in decentralized data. The approach employs novel gradient compression techniques and dynamic node participation strategies to minimize communication overhead while preserving model accuracy. We will leverage our prior work on scalable distributed optimization to architect a modular system prototype, enabling empirical evaluation across diverse real-world datasets.'})

arguments.content: We propose a hybrid federated learning framework that integrates adaptive communication protocols with personalized model updates to efficiently mitigate statistical heterogeneity in decentralized data. The approach employs novel gradient compression techniques and dynamic node participation strategies to minimize communication overhead while preserving model accuracy. We will leverage our prior work on scalable distributed optimization to architect a modular system prototype, enabling empirical evaluation across diverse real-world datasets.
